edits.match: It works within about an hour, is taken once a day and is sold without prescription, but it is the most sedating of the modern antihistamines and is an add-on, never a substitute for adrenaline, in anaphylaxis.
edits.replacement: It works within about an hour, is taken once a day and is sold without prescription, but it can cause drowsiness in some people and is an add-on, never a substitute for adrenaline, in anaphylaxis.
edits.reason: UNSAFE: 'the most sedating of the modern antihistamines' is an overstated absolute not in the NHS source, which says only that drowsiness is possible although cetirizine is classed as non-drowsy.

edits.match: Feeling sleepy or tired is the most common effect (more than 1 in 10 people, and more than with loratadine, desloratadine or fexofenadine)
edits.replacement: Feeling sleepy or tired (about 1 in 10 people, and more than with loratadine or fexofenadine)
edits.reason: WRONG: the frequency was changed from the pre-patch 'about 1 in 10' to 'more than 1 in 10' and 'the most common effect' added, neither supported by the NHS excerpt; restored to the pre-patch figure.

notes: Line-by-line check. NHS excerpts support: headaches, dry mouth, feeling sick, dizziness, diarrhoea; drowsiness possible despite non-drowsy label with driving/cycling avoided; alcohol heightens effects; anaphylaxis very rare. No dose figure added (once a day matches pre-patch 'lasts 24 hours'). Adrenaline-first in anaphylaxis, QT prolongation with withdrawn agents and driving/alcohol cautions predate the patch. Severe itching on stopping after long use and 'use only as long as needed' are NHS common-questions content (general knowledge). Eye drops and IV form (US) are accurate product facts. No protected field changed.
